title: The Beinecke Cipher (Voynich) Manuscript
supported_claims: Official manuscript custody and access record; text and illustrations constitute distinct evidence.
limitations: Catalog descriptions are not a decipherment or proof of everyday use.
voynich_implication: Anchor manuscript identity and image access; do not turn illustrative section names into translated content.

title: Voynich MS - Text Analysis - Transliteration of the Text
supported_claims: Transcription alphabets encode different choices about glyph decomposition and uncertainty.
limitations: A Latin transcription character is not established as an original grapheme or phoneme; mutable web documentation.
voynich_implication: Evaluate hypotheses across transcription views and preserve ambiguous readings rather than force one alphabet.

title: The Linguistics of the Voynich Manuscript
supported_claims: Review argues for meaningful language and surveys statistical linguistic approaches.
limitations: Full author-hosted PDF exceeded the web fetch limit in this pass; detailed evidence is separately read in D04, not attributed to this abstract.
voynich_implication: Treat language as a serious hypothesis, not settled ground truth.

title: Character Entropy in Modern and Historical Texts: Comparison Metrics for an Undeciphered Manuscript
supported_claims: Comparison corpus includes 311 Wikipedia languages, 18 historical texts, multiple transcription and scribal partitions.
Unusually constrained within-word character placement persists across tested transcription choices.
limitations: Not exhaustive over languages or encodings; unusual entropy does not identify a cipher.
Scribe, Currier class and illustration category are correlated.
voynich_implication: Use diplomatic historical corpora and factor scribal/layout differences out of language comparisons.

title: Topic Modeling in the Voynich Manuscript
supported_claims: Text-only page clusters align with combinations of scribal and illustration categories.
Authors explicitly allow similarity to reflect meaning, encipherment, or both.
limitations: Bag-of-words topic alignment is not recovered semantics; section-dependent meaningless generators remain competitors.
voynich_implication: Use cross-scribe same-topic comparisons and same-scribe cross-topic comparisons wherever overlap permits.

title: Keywords and Co-Occurrence Patterns in the Voynich Manuscript: An Information-Theoretic Analysis
supported_claims: Word-distribution information and co-occurrence reveal organization beyond globally shuffled text.
limitations: Calling co-occurrence semantic requires an additional assumption; global shuffling is a weak alternative to structured nonsemantic generation.
voynich_implication: Require section-aware and copy/mutate null generators before semantic claims.

title: A possible generating algorithm of the Voynich manuscript: accompanying self-citation materials
sections_read: Generated text and similarity graph inventory
supported_claims: Authors supply a self-citation generator and outputs accompanying their published nonsemantic-generation argument.
limitations: This pass inspected repository materials, not the full publisher paper or executable implementation.
Statistical resemblance does not prove historical production or meaninglessness.
voynich_implication: Use a faithful pinned generator as an adversarial negative control, not as an accepted explanation.

title: The Naibbe cipher: a substitution cipher that encrypts Latin and Italian as Voynich Manuscript-like ciphertext
supported_claims: Author provides reversible verbose homophonic encryption and decryption with Voynich-like statistics.
limitations: Publisher PDF fetch failed in this pass; repository abstract and implementation inventory were read.
Not a Voynich decipherment and not a match to all manuscript properties.
voynich_implication: Use as a difficult semantic positive control paired against nonsemantic generators.

title: Decoding Anagrammed Texts Written in an Unknown Language and Script
supported_claims: Models substitution plus within-word anagramming, optional missing vowels, and language selection from supplied comparison texts.
limitations: Voynich Hebrew suggestion is conditional on this flexible family; synthetic accuracy is not manuscript decipherment.
Changing order, restoring vowels and dictionary search increase chances of plausible accidental output.
voynich_implication: Every added decoder freedom must be costed and evaluated against wrong-language and nonsemantic controls.

title: What We Know About The Voynich Manuscript
supported_claims: Documents linguistic-looking and atypical properties at different scales, including line-edge distributions.
limitations: Descriptive similarities do not uniquely choose linguistic or hoax accounts; some historical statements predate later scholarship.
voynich_implication: Model physical line position explicitly and avoid using one statistic as a language detector.

title: The Copiale Cipher
supported_claims: Successful decipherment combined context clustering, language evidence, human corrections and a reusable mapping with homophones, multiletter symbols, spaces and a repeat operator.
limitations: Early choice of informative versus null-like symbols was wrong; human expertise was central.
This historical success is not a ciphertext-only neural result.
voynich_implication: Mixed typed operations are a realistic control family; demand globally reusable rules rather than sentence improvisation.

title: Can Sequence-to-Sequence Models Crack Substitution Ciphers?
supported_claims: Frequency-rank encoding addresses changing symbol identities in supervised random-key substitution tasks.
Model is trained on ciphertext/plaintext pairs and can accommodate character edits.
limitations: No language label is different from no language training; substitution is a specified family.
voynich_implication: Baseline raw-symbol training against canonicalized representations; calibrate edit tolerance before manuscript use.

title: Decipherment as Regression: Solving Historical Substitution Ciphers by Learning Symbol Recurrence Relations
supported_claims: First-occurrence indexing removes arbitrary cipher symbol names; training uses two million synthetic homophonic pairs.
English-only zero-shot Latin example has 45.14% symbol error; three manual interventions reduce this to 3.89%.
limitations: Recurrence preserves equality structure, not arbitrary homophone regrouping or cipher-family invariance.
Supervised plaintext exposure and human intervention materially affect transfer claims.
voynich_implication: Most direct candidate for testing whether our failed unseen-key transfer comes from representation rather than insufficient size.

title: ALICE: An Interpretable Neural Architecture for Generalization in Substitution Ciphers
supported_claims: Encoder transformer pools by symbol; optional Gumbel-Sinkhorn head produces inspectable permutations.
Training preserves spaces/punctuation and supplies plaintext/ciphertext pairs under random bijections.
limitations: Bijective head is less accurate; dynamic embeddings do not improve the reported comparison.
Layerwise early exits are not causal identification of an algorithm; a bijection is unverified for Voynich.
voynich_implication: Borrow symbol-consistent outputs as a controlled solver variant, not a manuscript-wide assumption.

title: Unsupervised Cipher Cracking Using Discrete GANs
supported_claims: Learns mappings between unpaired plaintext and ciphertext distributions using adversarial and cycle losses.
limitations: Unpaired still includes plaintext samples; cycle consistency does not uniquely identify historically correct semantics.
voynich_implication: Defer until candidate language/channel assumptions and null calibration are fixed.

title: Neural Decipherment via Minimum-Cost Flow: From Ugaritic to Linear B
supported_claims: Joint sequence alignment and global flow constraints identify cognates using known related-language vocabularies.
limitations: 67.3% refers to Linear B cognates in the evaluated setting, not complete free translation.
Known related language and vocabulary proximity are substantial supervision.
voynich_implication: Use global coverage and correspondence constraints only in a separately labeled cognate hypothesis.

title: Deciphering Undersegmented Ancient Scripts Using Phonetic Prior
supported_claims: Joint segmentation/cognate alignment uses IPA geometry, monotone edits, coverage and sound-preservation regularizers.
Language comparison need not assume one predetermined closest relative.
limitations: Requires supplied known-language vocabularies and an alphabetic lost-script assumption; not arbitrary cipher recovery.
voynich_implication: A useful segmentation/noisy-channel template, with phonetic priors switched off unless evidence supports them.

title: Decipherment of Lost Ancient Scripts as Combinatorial Optimisation using Coupled Simulated Annealing
supported_claims: Explicit k-permutation representation accommodates null, one-to-many and many-to-one sign mappings.
limitations: Benchmark concerns cognate matching with known-language lexica, not unconstrained sentence decipherment.
Greater mapping flexibility increases ambiguity.
voynich_implication: A transparent bounded-search baseline for multigraph channels; charge every extra operation.

title: Decipherment of Historical Manuscript Images
supported_claims: Combines unsupervised image segmentation, glyph clustering and probabilistic decipherment on known historical ciphers.
limitations: Copiale nomenclators are removed; Borg plaintext fragments are removed; evaluation conditions simplify full manuscripts.
Language-model and cipher assumptions supply information absent in Voynich.
voynich_implication: Retain alternative glyph hypotheses jointly with channel inference; benchmark simplified cases transparently.

title: Joint Transcription and Decryption of Images of Encrypted Handwritten Documents: A Comparison with the Traditional Pipeline
supported_claims: Direct image-to-German training is compared with transcription/decryption pipeline on Copiale; synthetic inputs are generated using the known cipher.
limitations: Supervised known-key Copiale rendering is not discovery of an unknown script or language.
No pretrained weights does not mean absence of plaintext supervision.
voynich_implication: Use for an image-noise calibration benchmark; do not train direct Voynich-to-English outputs.

title: Attention-Augmented LSTMs for Automatic Homophonic Ciphertext Decipherment
supported_claims: Every ciphertext code has the same plaintext value across the dataset; keys vary only in chosen subsets.
Near-perfect reported results concern this shared-pool supervised task.
limitations: This is explicitly not general homophonic cryptanalysis with independently reassigned keys.
voynich_implication: Reject headline accuracy as evidence for unseen-key recovery; preserve as an easy diagnostic control only.

title: DreamCoder: Growing generalizable, interpretable knowledge with wake-sleep Bayesian program learning
supported_claims: Neurally guided search learns reusable program libraries scored by task likelihood and a description-length prior.
limitations: Requires a domain-specific language and evaluable task likelihood; no Voynich decipherment demonstrated. Same work as T13.
voynich_implication: Use as inspiration for explicit bounded decoder-program search; minimal programs need not encode meaning.

title: A Generative Grammar Underlying the Voynich Manuscript, the Pastiche Hypothesis: Evidence from Large Language Models
supported_claims: Proposes probabilistic grammar and LLM-assisted botanical comparison as evidence for structured pastiche.
Section 9 starts from independent uniformly distributed initials; displayed alphabet-size references are inconsistent.
limitations: Metadata conflict: arXiv identifier has 2609 prefix while page reports submission 2026-07-28.
Rejecting that simple null does not reject language or encipherment; visual similarity is not a decipherment.
voynich_implication: Reproduce only under empirical, section-aware nulls and independent image annotation before taking the conclusion seriously.

title: The Voice But Not the Song: A Shorthand Hypothesis and the Statistical Fingerprint of the Voynich Manuscript
supported_claims: Author proposes Italian syllabic shorthand and reports permutation-tested candidate words while explicitly denying complete decipherment.
limitations: Full optimization/search degrees of freedom and permutation-selection pipeline not audited here.
Author index labels March 2026; retrieved PDF says April 2026; no frozen version identifier located.
voynich_implication: Independent replication lead only; rerun the complete selection pipeline for every null and language.

title: The Voynich manuscript: Symbol roles revisited
supported_claims: Analyzes symbol recurrence intervals and proposed ligature roles across Voynich and comparison texts.
limitations: Dependence and nonstationarity can affect recurrence statistics; ligature candidates are not decoded values.
voynich_implication: Include transcriber-sensitive segmentation and section-conditioned controls when proposing glyph roles.
